newsitem.title: UK: Cookson gains after top-end results.
newsitem.headline: Cookson gains after top-end results.

text.p: Shares in speciality industrial materials group Cookson Group Plc rose in pre-market trade on Thursday, after results at the top end of expectations coupled with a modestly upbeat trading statement.
The stock was up 7-1/2p at 222 by 0719 GMT, extending a rally from the year's low of 181p set on July 10.
"The numbers were at the top end of the range and the outlook is pretty good," said one market-maker in the stock.

Dealers said the market had also welcomed management changes at the group, with chairman Robert Malpas retiring from the company to be replaced by current chief executive Richard Oster -- in turn replaced by current group managing director Stephen Howard.

Headline pre-tax profit before exceptionals were little changed at 85.4 million stg in the six moths ended June 1997, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range between 82.5 million stg and 85.0 million.
After one-off items, pre-tax profits rose 23 percent -- because last year's were boosted by one-time items -- while excluding currency effects, the pre-tax figure was up 35 percent.

Oster said he believed the group had regained momentum following a pause in 1996. Assuming exchange rates prevailing in the first half, he expected results for the year to be in line with expectations.
"The engineered products, advanced refractories and plastics divisions all performed well in the first half and enter the second half with sound prospects for further growth," he said.
